item.title: FMCSA overhauls vetting of truckers’ ELDs
item.description: Regulators aim to eliminate non-compliant, loophole-exploiting ELD equipment with a more rigorous vetting process.

item.title: Rail freight stays ahead of year-ago traffic
item.description: Freight on U.S. railroads year-to-date stayed ahead of 2024 levels even as intermodal and carload shipments were weaker in the latest weekly data.

item.title: Amazon Freight highlights steady, tech-driven growth in transportation
item.description: At this year’s F3: Future of Freight Festival, Amazon Freight General Manager Ari Silkey offered a detailed look at how Amazon’s transportation network has evolved.

item.title: DOT kicks 3,000 truck driver trainers off registry
item.description: FMCSA is cracking down on illegal CDL training by banning thousands of providers and warning 4,000 more that they risk getting banned as well.

item.title: XPO’s Q4 progressing as expected
item.description: XPO’s fourth-quarter update showed less-than-truckload trends largely in line with the company's prior guidance.

item.title: Inside DOT's New ELD Approval Overhaul, What Changed and Why It Matters
item.description: The FMCSA announced Monday a "complete overhaul" of the ELD approval process, implementing pre-publication vetting. This comes after the agency has revoked 308 devices from the approved list.

item.title: 10 Roads Express to shut down operations, end USPS contracts
item.description: 10 Roads Express has notified employees that it will wind down all operations over the next 60 days.

item.title: ArcBest stems revenue declines in November, margin hurdles remain
item.description: ArcBest reported improvement in revenue trends during November but reiterated its expectation for margin erosion in the fourth quarter.

item.title: The EV Truck Reality Check and Why Edison Motors' Hybrid Might Be What Actually Works
item.description: Edison Motors' diesel-electric hybrid trucks prove EVs can work in trucking when you build around operational realities rather than regulatory fantasies. That's the kind of practical engineering that deserves attention.

item.title: Trump Administration Purges 3,000 CDL Schools From Federal Registry
item.description: After 25 years of documented CDL fraud schemes producing 6,000+ fraudulent licenses and at least 13 deaths, FMCSA finally removed 3,000 training providers from the federal registry. The problem? Another 36,000 providers remain unvalidated, operating on the same honor system that enabled Operation Safe Road, Larex Incorporated, and the Massachusetts golden handshake scheme.
